messages:
maria: Heads-up — while validating streamed responses I noticed throughput drop (~18%) on short-turn chats. Profiler shows a lot of tiny flushes when KV-cache hit ratio is high; I think batching heuristic is timing out too often.

aj: Can you paste the profiler output and which model/kernel this was on?

maria: Quick extract from profiler run (vicuna-13b):
```
model: redwood-vicuna-13b
kernel: f16-gemm
avg_batch_size: 3.2
flushes_per_min: 145
kv_cache_hit_ratio: 0.78
avg_token_latency_ms: 12.5
streaming_flush_due_to_timeout_pct: 61.7
```
Basically we form tiny batches (1-4) because token_budget_target is small and requests hit cache so they produce few new tokens; the max_wait fires and causes partial-decode scheduling overhead.

kevin: For small batches the f16-gemm kernel has overhead from kernel-launchs + small-matrix inefficiencies. On my microbench for seq<=64 & batch<=4, the 'kv-opt' path is ~20% faster. Also current continuous-batching settings are: token_budget_target=32, max_wait_ms=10, queue_policy="size_based" — not ideal for streaming.

maria: Right now our streaming routes use token_budget_target=32. When kv_hit is high, new token generation per request is tiny so batches never reach that target and just flush on timeout. That makes kernel selection and launch overhead dominate.

lucy: Suggestion: switch queue_policy -> "age_and_size" so older requests are prioritized, increase token_budget_target for streaming routes (64), and add a `streaming_min_tokens` threshold (e.g., 4) to avoid flushing for tiny single-token bursts. Also add metric `partial_decode_sched_count`.

aj: Agreed. Also kernel-fallback rule: if batch_size < 6 && kv_cache_hit_ratio > 0.6 -> pick 'kv-opt' kernel. Will need microbench to validate.

perf-bot: CI perf run 1766999000 reported -15% p90 throughput on streaming tests (vicuna-13b) vs baseline.

maria: Plan for tonight's perf job (A/B):
1) queue_policy = "age_and_size"
2) token_budget_target = 64 for streaming routes
3) streaming_min_tokens = 4
4) kernel_fallback: if batch < 6 && kv_hit > 0.6 -> 'kv-opt'
5) amortize KV lookup per-batch (one lookup per batch, not per-request) behind a feature flag
I'll run a 4h perf run and post results.

kevin: Also add tracing for `kv_hit_ratio` per-request and `batch_level_kv_lookups` metric. We should ensure we don't accidentally change correctness for partial prefix merges.

aj: One more: partial-decode scheduling currently creates a separate decode task per flush. We should coalesce partial-decode tasks when they finish within a short window (e.g., 3ms) to reduce kernel churn.

maria: Good call. I'll enable coalescing + the other changes behind a feature flag. Target: recover the 18% throughput loss and reduce streaming flushes by ~40%.

lucy: If perf looks good, let's rollout as a canary (5% traffic) with alerts on token-level latency, p95 tail, and error-rate.

aj: I'll own the canary config + runbook.

perf-bot: perf job 1767007000 finished: A/B results (streaming vicuna-13b) -> throughput +22% vs baseline, p95 latency -8%, partial-decode_sched_count -43%, kernel_fallback activated for ~34% of small batches.

maria: Nice! Uploading the perf graphs to the perf dashboard and enabling canary for 5%. Will watch metrics. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

kevin: If we see any regressions on long-turn chats we might want to relax token_budget_target back down for non-streaming routes.

maria: Agreed — config will be per-route. Closing this thread once canary looks stable.
